symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: act_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character with a code of F000 or more, which is how the register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept Symbol-font characters typed as text as private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. act_convert_sym.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0B7 bullet to "•"; also · × − ≤ ≥ ° ′ — ÷ ±) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: Only bullets. Two Symbol bullets (w:sym F0B7) were dropped from the s 22P (1) list (Heritage Act 2004; Urban Forest Act 2023); 23 bullets kept as U+F0B7 (the middle s 22P item, the s 48 (2) (a) (ii) and s 48 (3) examples, and the 17 terms of the Dictionary note 2 list) are now "•". 26 lines changed (377-379, 699-701, 708-709, 1470-1486); the notice header and line structure are kept exactly, and a diff against the first deposit shows no other change. The same Word file (sha256 186f3433...a839) was reconverted.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: baseline-2026-11 reads s 48 (2), (3) but none of its values rests on the example bullets; s 22P and the Dictionary note are outside its scope
